title: Why IKEA makes you build it yourself 🔧
subject: furniture
description:
Do you love the furniture you built yourself? 👇

Why does IKEA sell flat-pack furniture you have to assemble? It started with a table that wouldn't fit in a car, and it pays off twice: lower costs and the IKEA effect.

Sources: IKEA Museum ("Flatpacks"), Dezeen ("IKEA relaunches first flat-pack table", 2013), Wallpaper ("Ikea leaf table"), Norton, Mochon & Ariely, Journal of Consumer Psychology (2012) "The IKEA effect: When labor leads to love"
tags: why does ikea make you build it yourself

scenes.text: IKEA's smartest trick is making you do the work.
In 1956, an IKEA designer couldn't fit a table in his car, so he took the legs off.
Flat boxes fit more furniture in every truck, and less breaks.
And you assemble it for free.
But here's the strange part. Building it makes you love it more.
In a 2012 study, people bid 63% more for boxes they built than for identical prebuilt ones. So when that wobbly shelf feels priceless, remember:
